title: How many days are in four calendar years?
description: With a leap day every fourth year, the video counts the days in four calendar years and compares them with four trips of the Earth round the Sun.
teaching_notes: One idea: four calendar years have one leap day, and four trips of the Earth are four times the decimal number of days. Watch for children who forget the leap day.

source: With a leap day every 4th year, how many days are in 4 calendar years? How many days does the Earth take for 4 revolutions?
video_script.why: The child knows a leap year has an extra day but has not yet compared four calendar years with four trips of the Earth.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four calendar years with one leap day, against four trips of the Earth of three hundred and sixty five point two four two two days each
video_script.anchor: Four calendar years with one leap day, against four trips of the Earth round the Sun
video_script.wrong_answer: one thousand four hundred and sixty days
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip counts four plain years of three hundred and sixty five days and forgets the leap day. One of the four years has an extra day.
video_script.payoff_line: The days in four years are now known.

final_answer.spoken: one thousand four hundred and sixty one days for the calendar, and one thousand four hundred and sixty point nine six eight eight days for the Earth

maths_rules: calendar: 4 × 365 = 1460, plus 1 leap day, so 1461 days
compare the parts after 1460: 1 against 0.9688, and 1 − 0.9688 = 0.0312
the calendar is ahead of the Earth by 0.0312 days
the slip: 1460 days leaves out the leap day
video_script.design: One idea: both totals begin with one thousand four hundred and sixty, so only the extra parts need comparing. Assumes multiplying a decimal by a counting number. Wrong idea: forgetting the leap day. The two totals stay hidden; one thousand four hundred and sixty one and one thousand four hundred and sixty point nine six eight eight appear only on the answer beat.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four times three hundred and sixty five is one thousand four hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then comes one leap day on top of that. We keep it separate for now.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the Earth's four trips have the same one thousand four hundred and sixty. They add four times the small part.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four times two tenths is eight tenths. Four times four hundredths is sixteen hundredths.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Four times two thousandths is eight thousandths. Four times two ten thousandths is eight ten thousandths.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Added together, these make zero point nine six eight eight.
